discussion_comments.comment_body:
the problem with this approach is that we'd be using the Queue to process entries in parallel, i.e. not what a queue normally does. To properly reuse the code (now in the queue) that processes an entry we should probably extract it from the Queue module and then refer to it both from the queue and from here.

If this is too complex for the scope of this task we might want to do it as a separate refactor.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
One thing in `concurrency` is that it makes difficult to not use anonymous functions. This could be fixed by changing:
```lua
function concurrency.with_worker_mutex(opts, fn)
```
to
```lua
function concurrency.with_worker_mutex(opts, fn, ...)
```

and

```lua
function concurrency.with_coroutine_mutex(opts, fn)
```
to
```lua
function concurrency.with_coroutine_mutex(opts, fn, ...)
```


Then the code here could  be changed from:
```lua
return concurrency.with_worker_mutex({
    name = POLL_INTERVAL_LOCK_KEY,
    timeout = 0,
    exptime = self.poll_interval - 0.001,
  }, function()
  return poll(self)
end)
```
to
```lua
return concurrency.with_worker_mutex({
    name = POLL_INTERVAL_LOCK_KEY,
    timeout = 0,
    exptime = self.poll_interval - 0.001,
}, poll, self)
```
Worth to consider that, but I am also fine if done later, if it feels scope creep.

at the moment `with_worker_mutex` passes exactly one argument (`elapsed`) to `fn`: https://github.com/Kong/kong/blob/4adb6772a13e036f770ef6110c665e663db8cade/kong/concurrency.lua#L59

If we change it as you say and still keep `elapsed` as one of the arguments to `fn` (the first?) then we should always remember that `fn` won't only receive the args that are passed as varargs to `with_worker_mutex`, which would also be inconsistent to how things work in `with_coroutine_mutex`. What do you think @bungle ?

final logic of notify()
```
notify
-> fut.start
  -> socket: call
    -> 
-- asynchronously start executing a RPC, _node_id is not
-- needed for this implementation, but it is important
-- for concentrator socket, so we include it just to keep
-- the signature consistent
function _M:call(node_id, method, params, callback)
  assert(node_id == self.node_id)

  local id

  -- notification has no callback or id
  if callback then
    id = self:_get_next_id()
    self.interest[id] = callback
  end

  return self:push_request({
    jsonrpc = jsonrpc.VERSION,
    method = method,
    params = params,
    id = id,
  })
end
```

discussion_comments.comment_body: I.e, if we have no error but the version still does not match, we count it as 1 trial; if it's a real failure (internal or external), we still count it as 1 trial.
